segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet planetarium ventilation hum] [softly] Sit or lie comfortably. Let the eyes rest behind closed lids and imagine entering a small planetarium after dark.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the body supported first... feet, seat, hands, and the natural movement of breath. Grounding is the floor beneath every constellation.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Bring gentle attention to the space between the eyebrows. Keep the physical eyes soft and level, without trying to look upward.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine a violet lens there, no larger than a coin. It does not burn or push; it simply gathers scattered light.
[soft, slow, warm voice] With each easy inhale, the lens becomes clear. With each exhale, unnecessary effort falls away like dust from a projector.
[soft, slow, warm voice] A thought may paint a comet across the dome. Notice it, then return to the quiet lens at the centre.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If you see darkness, colour, patterns, or nothing in particular, all are acceptable. The practice is attention, not special effects.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest with the point of focus while the rest of the face remains spacious... jaw loose, tongue resting, forehead smooth.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] If pressure or strain appears, widen attention to the whole head or open the eyes. Comfort is more important than intensity.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the violet lens float in a much larger field of awareness, like one friendly planet among uncountable dark miles.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release the image. Keep only the calm precision of returning whenever the mind wandered.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the hands and feet again. Notice the room as the planetarium slowly raises its ordinary lights.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes when ready. Carry the lens as a metaphor for clear attention, not something you must keep seeing.
